solutions.title: Evaluate the inner sum first
solutions.explanation:
For a fixed \(i\), the inner sum contains \(100\) copies of \(i\), together with the integers from \(1\) through \(100\). First compute
\[
1+2+\cdots+100=\frac{100(1+100)}{2}=5050.
\]
Therefore
\[
\sum_{j=1}^{100}(i+j)=100i+5050.
\]
Now sum over the \(100\) possible values of \(i\). The \(100i\) terms contribute \(100\cdot5050\), and the constant \(5050\) also appears \(100\) times. Thus
\[
\sum_{i=1}^{100}(100i+5050)
=100\cdot5050+100\cdot5050
=1{,}010{,}000.
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{1{,}010{,}000}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
